commit.message:
scripts: add command to lint submodules

Add make lint-module to lint every non-tools Go submodule, or a single module selected with module=<path>.

Reuse the standard Docker cache and Git worktree mounts, preserve nested module paths, forward worker limits, and report all failing modules after the complete pass. The command remains opt-in and is not added to CI yet.

commit.message:
kvdb: test bucket lookups after create and delete

Add tests covering lookups of buckets that are created, deleted and
re-created within the same transaction, and lookups across committed and
rolled back transactions. These run against all backends to make sure
the SQL backend's bucket id cache behaves like bbolt and etcd.

We also test the cache itself, making sure that a repeated lookup isn't
sent to the database and that the cache stays bounded.

commit.message:
kvdb/sqlbase: cache nested bucket ids within a transaction

Every nested bucket lookup in the SQL kvdb backend is a query, whereas
with bbolt it's an in-memory lookup. Callers are written with the bbolt
cost in mind and resolve the same bucket path over and over within a
transaction. btcwallet's address manager for example resolves its scope
bucket for every address and account it reads, so the majority of the
queries issued by wallet calls such as WalletBalance are lookups of
bucket ids that were already looked up in the same transaction.

We now cache bucket ids, including buckets that were found not to
exist, for the lifetime of a transaction. As a transaction reads from a
single snapshot, a bucket id can only change through the transaction's
own writes. Creating a bucket updates the cache. Deleting a bucket
clears it, as the delete cascades to an unknown set of sub-buckets and
sqlite may hand out the ids of deleted buckets again. The cache is
bounded, as transactions that walk a large number of buckets don't
benefit from it.

commit.message:
lnwallet/chanfunding: allow maxFeeRatio above 1.0

Raise the upper bound on maxFeeRatio in sanityCheckFee from 1.0 to a
hard ceiling of 5.0, so that an RPC caller can opt in to a fee that
exceeds the transaction's total output value.

The concrete caller is the taproot-assets daemon, which funds PSBTs
that anchor asset outputs through walletrpc.FundPsbt with a ratio of
5.0 (see lndservices.DefaultPsbtMaxFeeRatio). Those transactions spend
asset-bearing UTXOs whose BTC value sits near dust because the value
they carry lives at the asset level, so in a busy fee market the fee
legitimately dwarfs the BTC output value and the 1.0 bound would fail
the funding outright. The ceiling is set to exactly that demonstrated
requirement and can be raised if another use case appears;
TestNearDustReAnchorFeeRatio pins the realistic re-anchor flow as
needing a ratio above 1.0 and fitting under 5.0.

Note that this is independent of the deterministic second-level HTLC
work in the rest of this series: the CPFP anchor sweep goes through the
sweeper (Sweeper.SweepInput with a budget), not through FundPsbt, so
nothing in this PR exercises the relaxed bound. It is carried here
because the companion taproot-assets series depends on it, and it can
be split into its own PR on request.

Every internal funding flow keeps passing DefaultMaxFeeRatio, ratios
above 1.0 are logged by FundPsbt so the opt-in is auditable, and the
new ceiling still rejects nonsensical values.

build: cancel unfinished CI runs when a PR is closed

Once a PR is merged (or closed) its CI result no longer matters, but
a run that is still in progress keeps occupying runners, often for the
better part of an hour due to the itests.

Add a workflow triggered on pull_request_target closed that cancels
every unfinished run of the main CI workflow triggered by the PR's head
commit. pull_request_target is used so the token has actions: write
even for PRs opened from forks. No PR code is checked out or executed.

A PR that is closed and quickly reopened gets a fresh run for the same
head commit. To never cancel it, the handler bails out if the PR is
open again by the time it runs and only considers runs that were
created before the close event.

Only main.yml runs are targeted on purpose: the backport workflow is
triggered by the very same closed event and shares the head commit, so
a broader match would cancel it.

commit.message:
build: skip CI for docs-only changes and run a fast subset on drafts

Every push to a PR currently runs the full CI matrix regardless of what
changed or whether the PR is still being iterated on. Introduce two
measures to cut down on wasted runners while keeping all jobs in
parallel, so a single run still reports as many failures as possible:

1. A ci-gate job runs first and detects documentation-only PRs, i.e.
   PRs that only touch files under docs/ or markdown files. Renamed
   files are checked under both their old and new name so that moving
   a source file into docs/ doesn't count as a documentation change.
   The cheap commit and release notes checks always run. The way the
   other jobs are skipped depends on whether they have a matrix:

   - Non-matrix jobs (static checks, lint) and non-required jobs are
     skipped at the job level. A skipped job still reports its status,
     so the required checks in branch protection are satisfied.
   - Matrix jobs with required legs (unit tests, cross compilation,
     pinned dependencies, basic itests) are kept instantiated and skip
     their steps instead, in the same way the no-itest label already
     works. A job-level condition is evaluated before the matrix is
     expanded, so a skipped matrix job would never report the per-leg
     check names that branch protection requires and the PR would
     stay blocked.

   All job-level conditions use !cancelled() so that a failure of the
   gate job itself results in the full CI running rather than
   everything being skipped.

2. Draft PRs only run a fast subset: static checks, lint, the pinned
   dependency check, the non-race unit test legs and the basic itests
   (18-22 min per leg). The large itests (up to 86 min per leg),
   Windows and macOS itests, cross compilation, the race unit legs
   (47-56 min) and the backwards compatibility test are skipped until
   the PR is marked ready for review. ready_for_review and
   converted_to_draft are added to the pull_request trigger types so
   that changing the draft state triggers a run with the right subset;
   the concurrency group cancels the previous one.

Push and merge_group runs carry no PR and always run everything.
